sections.name: CanonicalTable
sections.title: Table layout for canonical slides
sections.what: Draws a canonical slide as a table. Column headings come from the table definition, and each cell shows the stored bullet at its index with a clickable link, reference numbers and an Edited Unverified wording note. The table is read-only; edits happen through the text editor.
sections.why: The comment says every cell is the stored bullet at that index, edited via the bullet number name.
sections.watch_out: A cell whose index has no bullet shows a dash, so broken table data appears as blanks rather than an error. The reference numbers here come from a different helper than the one in CanonicalBody.

sections.name: ClaimSources, PROFILE_LABEL
sections.title: Sources by claim panel
sections.what: Lists each claim on the page with a short label, its text, up to three source buttons, a link to more references, and a source link when one exists. Claims without evidence are marked Unsupported, and calculation or methodology claims link to their basis. Profile codes are turned into readable labels such as Pillar and Subdriver.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reviewer see at a glance which claims lack evidence. Not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A claim is marked Unsupported unless it has evidence, a link, a basis or an editorial flag, so a missing flag shows as unsupported by default.

sections.name: related, LLTextEdit
sections.title: Related pages and text edit type
sections.what: Finds other standard pages linked to the current one, such as a pillar's sub-drivers, a sub-driver's examples, or a project's pages, by matching shared IDs. Also defines the shape of a text edit: slide ID, element ID and new text.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reviewer move between parent and child pages.
sections.watch_out: Links appear only when IDs match exactly, so a missing ID on a page removes its related links.

sections.name: LLSaveEdits
sections.title: Save contract for edits
sections.what: Defines what a save function must do: accept a list of edits and return either nothing on success or an error message.
sections.why: The comment says drafts are kept when a save fails, so the reviewer does not lose typed text.
sections.watch_out: Returning anything other than an empty result on success will show as an error.

sections.name: TextEditor
sections.title: Slide text editor
sections.what: A collapsible panel with a text box for the title, subtitle and each bullet. It tracks changes as drafts, checks them against the same rules the server uses, then calls the save function. If the save fails, the drafts stay in place and the error is shown. It also notes that citations stay as originally recorded.
sections.why: The comment says the check matches the server and export, rejecting the whole batch when any edit breaks the rules.
sections.watch_out: The client-side check must change whenever the server rules change, or edits will be accepted in one place and rejected in the other.

sections.name: amendedFields
sections.title: Reviewer amendment finder
sections.what: Compares the stored original wording with the current text for the title, subtitle and bullets on a slide. It returns only items whose text has actually changed, so the warning can show what was amended.
sections.why: The comment says it reads the saved original wording record on the stored slide.
sections.watch_out: Only keys named in the bullet pattern are compared, so other recorded changes are ignored.

sections.name: LLSlideView (part 1)
sections.title: Main slide review screen (part 1)
sections.what: The main review screen. It builds the pages, tracks which page is shown, lets arrow keys move between pages (but not while typing), and keeps the current page within range. It shows the instruction line, the preview frame, previous and next buttons, a Go to drop-down, related-page buttons and a thumbnail strip where thumbnails cannot be clicked.
sections.why: Likely reason: keyboard and thumbnail navigation make long decks quicker to review. Not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The page position is clamped to the list length, so a shorter page list does not cause an error.

sections.name: LLSlideView (part 2)
sections.title: Main slide review screen (part 2)
sections.what: Shows the Full slide text panel, a warning when reviewer amendments exist, the text editor for standard and summary pages, the claim sources panel (not for divider pages), up to 12 evidence buttons, and a footer. The footer says standard pages show every bullet and that the exported PPTX is authoritative.
sections.why: The footer wording shows that on-screen text is a review copy and the exported file is the official version.
sections.watch_out: Evidence buttons beyond the first 12 are reached only through the single all-references link.

summary: The slide-by-slide review screen for a lessons analysis. It shows each page as it will look, with clickable sources and an optional text editor.
purpose: Let a reviewer read and check each page of the lessons deck alongside its evidence, and optionally edit slide text.
why: The screen states that the exported PPTX is authoritative, so this view is a review aid. Otherwise the reason is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Builds a list of pages from the saved slides and recipe. 2. Shows the current page as a scaled preview with its evidence references. 3. Arrow keys and buttons move between pages. A drop-down and related-page buttons jump to linked pages. 4. Below the preview, shows full slide text, a warning for reviewer-amended wording, an optional text editor, claim sources and evidence buttons. Only sections 21 to 28 were provided; sections 1 to 20 were not in the packet.
inputs: Slides, the recipe (facts, pillars, projects), callbacks for opening citations, a check for whether a fact can be cited, an edit callback, and a save callback.
outputs: The review screen. Citation requests go to the open callback. Edits go to the save callback, which sends them to the server.
risks: Most of the file was not provided, so the page-building logic is unconfirmed. The editor applies the same rules as the server, so the two must stay aligned. The superscript helper here is different from the one in CanonicalBody.
debug: If pages are missing, check the slides passed in and the page builder (not provided). If a fact button is disabled, check that the fact is in the recipe and has a direct citation. If saves fail, read the message in the edit panel and compare the rules with the server.
